## P.5 Findings

Severity as the task sets it: 3 a row broken in both runs or a feature that does not do what PRODUCT.md says, 2 a defect a seller meets, 1 cosmetic or a blob tier flake. The owner is the lane whose files carry the mechanism (PRODUCT.md 7.1).

1. Severity 3, B7 and B1. The default record of a deck made on this deployment is `generalAccess { mode: 'open', role: 'editor' }` (`packages/store/src/access-store.ts` `defaultGeneralAccessFor({ anonymousPrincipals: true })`, written by `recordNewDeck` for the anonymous creator), and `packages/chrome/src/dialogs/Share.tsx` line 824 reads `mode === 'open'` as legacy: the first stage draws "Anyone with the address can view (legacy)" with the sentence "Anyone with the address can open and edit this presentation." over the plain `/edit/<id>` address, no General access select (whose options are `restricted` and `link`), no role select, no owner row reading You, and Copy link copies the plain address; `share.get` on the window API and over HTTP with the bearer answers the same record at 0, 5 and 20 s (owner set, `createdBy` the anonymous principal), so the record exists and the word is the seam. A stranger's tab opens in editing mode and its write answers 401 (preview) or 409 (local). PRODUCT.md rank 3 says a deck from `/new` starts as Anyone with the link, Editor, with the tokenized general link in the field. The 28 rows of `core/share.spec.ts` read red on both tiers from this one root and the four `share.dialog.*` rows time out on the spec's opener (B1, B4). Fix: the default record's mode is `link` with the general link minted, or the dialog draws the `open` record as Anyone with the link, Editor over a minted link, whichever PRODUCT.md's decision (question 10) means; and `shareStage` passes the name prompt. Evidence: `product-p1-seller-share-dialog.png`, `product-p1-pass3-share.png`, `product-p1-pass3-preview.json`.
2. Severity 3, B5b with B7. File > Save as template on the blob tier answers "Saved the template <name> · Open gallery" and the gallery never lists it; `template.list` over HTTP on three instances lists `blank` and `gt-brand` alone (B5b's R6: the template lives in one instance's overlay). `templates.save.as-template` and `templates.save.same-name-replaces` are green on the memory tier and red on the deployment, and the two card rows and `templates.default.use-for-new` cascade or time out on both tiers (a cover read of the live clone, B4). PRODUCT.md 4.3 says the gallery lists the saved template under Your organisation. Evidence: `product-p1-marketer-preview.json` row 10, `product-p1-marketer-save-as-template.png`.
3. Severity 3, B5a and B6 with the integrator. A write's history label and the assistant's author do not reach the version log on either tier: after Colors > Primary the version row reads the time and You; after Accept on Make it shorter the row reads "You · 23 changes" with no Assist: label and no row named Assistant (`brand.colors.version-history-entry`, `assist.rewrite.card-accept-undo`, `assist.mark.chip-and-history`; integrator.md section 6 names the protocol field and the server side accept). Evidence: `product-p1-marketer-preview.json` row 3, `product-p1-assist-preview.json` row 4.
4. Severity 3, the integrator with B7. `versions.undo-restore` is red on both tiers and its mechanism moved: on the memory tier the restore lands at once (2 ms) and Cmd+Z does not bring the current version back, where the return round read the row green on the memory tier and red on the blob tier alone. A `versions` row is unparkable.
5. Severity 2, B2. Heading link corruption. In a heading run (the title slide's title, the split layout's h/text): type `sales@acme.com`, press Enter (the single line title commits by `text.title.enter-commits` and the address wraps as mailto), type `Renewal` (the session reopens with the whole text selected and the word replaces it, A1 rule 4): the stored text is `[Renewal](mailto:sales@acme.com)` while the session draws plain Renewal with no anchor; double click Renewal, Cmd+K (the URL field reads empty), type `acme.com/renewal`, Enter: the stored text becomes `[Renewal](https://acme.com/renewal)l](mailto:sales@acme.com)` and the heading renders `Renewall](mailto:sales@acme.com)` in the editor and the show. The body paragraph is clean under the same keys (Enter makes a new line; the stored text `[sales@acme.com](mailto:sales@acme.com)\n[Renewal](https://acme.com/renewal)`). Two mechanisms in `packages/viewer/src/InlineText.tsx` and `marks.ts`: the replacement of a fully linked selection inherits the link mark, and the link apply splices raw markup at plain offsets when the run carries a mark the session does not draw. Evidence: `product-p1-pass4-preview.json`, `product-p1-pass4-heading-after.png`, `product-p1-seller-show-entry.png`.
6. Severity 2, B2. Upload from computer lands the picture centred on the sheet (x 301 to 1300, y 169 to 731 on a 1600 by 900 sheet) and not in the body slot (`images.insert.centred-in-body` red on both tiers, 212 px off), and the first img draws 727 ms (the spec) and 1034 ms (the seller's hour, timed in the page) after the file is handed over against the 500 ms bound (`images.insert.instant-preview` red on the preview, green locally). The progress bar shows, no snackbar follows, the picture is selected, Add a caption works. Evidence: `product-p1-seller-hour-preview.json` row 11, `product-p1-seller-picture-uploaded.png`.
7. Severity 2, B2. Insert > Image > By URL places no picture within 20 s on either tier (`images.insert.by-url`; the row carries `parks`, so its two controls stay parked and it blocks nothing).
8. Severity 2, B7 with B1. The download snackbar never reads slide k of n during a PowerPoint export (`export.download.progress-per-slide`, B7's R4 deferral); the PDF's snackbar reads "Saved GT pitch for Acme.pdf" with Details as specified.
9. Severity 2, B7 with B3. `arrange.clipboard.paste-keeps-position` read red twice on the preview and green locally: a paste onto another slide from its stage showed the readout 280 by 180 and landed no object, in the shape of the lines setup's stale revision on the blob tier; a paste that vanishes is a defect a seller meets.
10. Severity 2, B1. `/new`'s skeleton did not draw and the editor was ready at 733 and 832 ms (past the 300 ms it is skipped under), so a seller sees the blank shell for most of a second (`decks.new.skeleton-one-frame`); the list view's rows are 33 px against 32 (`decks.card.edited-relative-time`, severity 1).
11. Severity 1, B1 with B4. `present.show.no-white-block`: the spec counts three or four elements painted paper in the bottom left outside the bar; the show's picture shows the slide's own paper reaching the corner and no block, and the bar fades to opacity 0 after 3.6 s. The spec names the elements or the product hides them.
12. Severity 2, B7. `deck.tailor` over HTTP on the memory tier answered `replacements: 0` on a deck holding five Acme while the editor's snackbar read "Tailored for Globex" with Undo (the integrator's finding stands there); on the preview by hand the same call answered 3 of 3, skipped the slide, moved one revision and the snackbar named the change with Undo, and the dialog by hand reads "2 places on 2 slides", skips, applies and undoes as one step.
13. Severity 2, B4 with B3. `slides.import.none-preselected` under enforce: the dialog lists no other presentation for the fresh principal within the driver's wait even after the driver's copy of the brand deck landed, and the imported slides then landed on the walk's deck after the row moved on, breaking `text.subtitle.double-click-type` behind it. The row was not driven by hand.
14. Severity 2, B1 with B7. The display name typed at the first Share does not reach the second browser's presence chip within 10 s on either tier (`share.name-prompt.first-share`); the prompt itself, its words and the save work by hand.
15. Severity 2, B2 with the export's owner. `formatting.alt-text.write-undo` on the memory tier: the description writes and Cmd+Z takes it back, and the Editable text export carries no `descr` for the walk's box (the integrator's open item).
16. Severity 1, B4 and the lanes named. Driver seams that read a working product red on both tiers: `brand.logo.replace-every-slide` (`.mark img` cannot match the `<img class="mark mark-picture">`), `brand.colors.role-tooltips` (the stepped hover; all six read by hand), `brand.footer.text` (the footer reads Confidential on the body slide and in the PDF's text by hand), `export.download.pptx-direct` (the spec waits for a dialog the direct row does not open; the table deck's dialog opens by hand), `decks.recent.drops-trashed` (a 90 s wait of the spec; the row drops the deck at once by hand), `present.presenter.sentence-case` (the disabled Previous arrow on the first slide).
17. Severity 1, B6 with B1. The Assist button's tooltip reads the name and the sentence with no key, where New slide's carries `Ctrl M` and PRODUCT.md 6.1 writes "Assist, Cmd+J" (RETURN.md section 4's tooltip rule); Cmd+J works.
18. Severity 1, B1. Version history's head button reads "Name current version" where PRODUCT.md 3.2 writes "Name this version"; the checkbox label "Only show named versions" wraps to three lines in the 320 px panel; the display name prompt a second browser meets on opening the deck is a bottom right card reading "How should others see you?" (the Share prompt reads "Your name, shown to collaborators" as specified).
19. Severity 1, the integrator with B1. Check step 27 over the whole matrix against the `vite preview` build on 4344 reads 65 failures and 11 skipped states, most of them one load entry on the /deck, /embed, /present and /decks list view cells; the step never ran in the return round, so whether these entries are the round's or the preview environment's is not known from this pass; the targeted /new and /edit audit reads the return round's six failures and nothing new.
20. Severity 1, the blob tier, recorded and not chased: the text section's reload reading a stale document (13 rows), the lines setup's stale revision (10 rows), `templates.save.same-name-replaces`'s cascade, `inbox.settings-persist` (parked), the large deck PowerPoint measurement row (P.4).

## P.1 Verdict

The tree does not ship yet under FOCUS.md 6.2 and RETURN.md section 1 rule 1, and the fix round moved the largest block of pass 1: 659 of 698 core rows are green in both runs (611 in pass 1), 29 are red or not driven in both (54), and no row green in both then is red in both now. The 22 rows of `core/share.spec.ts` that cascaded from the `open` record are green on both tiers (a deck from `/new` is Anyone with the link, Editor over a minted link; a stranger cannot edit; the copied link opens for a colleague as an editor and six typed words reach the first browser in 4.4 s by hand), `versions.undo-restore` and `versions.restore` are green on both tiers, the heading link corruption is gone, a picture lands in the body column in 10 ms, the skeleton and the 32 px rows read as specified, and the 85 slide Editable text PowerPoint arrives in 196 s where pass 1 read none within 600 s. What stands is one shape: the fix round built its server halves and wrote six requests to other lanes for the client and wiring halves, and none was made (B7's FR2, FR3, FR4 and FR6, B1's R16 to R18, B2's R-F1), which keeps nine rows red (the templates on the blob tier, the kit's and the assistant's history labels, the export's per slide words, the agent's tailor on the memory tier, the display name across browsers). Three share rows of an unparkable feature are red on both tiers by the new default's own edges (the address field is empty until Copy link, no owner row reads You), the assist's viewer sentence is not built, and the check chain is red at step 6 on the fix round's own file. The gate's blocking count is 11 rows on the preview and 14 locally; six of the eleven are driver seams pass 1 named that no fixer touched, which the ship step reads as the product's until the drivers change. ## P.5 Findings

Severity as the task sets it: 3 a row broken in both runs or a feature that does not do what PRODUCT.md says, 2 a defect a seller meets, 1 cosmetic or a blob tier flake. The owner is the lane whose files carry the mechanism (PRODUCT.md 7.1). Pass 1's twenty findings are each answered here or in P.4; a finding that stands names its pass 1 number in brackets. Closed by the fix round and read closed here: pass 1's 1 (the `open` record), 4 (`versions.undo-restore`), 5 (the heading link corruption), 6 (the picture's place and time), 7 (Image by URL), 9 (the vanishing paste), 10 (the skeleton and the 33 px rows), 13 (Import slides), 20 (the text and lines sections' blob tier flakes did not recur); 19 (check step 27) was not rerun.

1. Severity 2, B7 with the integrator (the allowlist's owner). The check chain's step 6 is red on the fix round's tree where pass 1 read it green: `node scripts/check.mjs --greps` fails on `packages/store/src/blob-templates.ts` lines 209 and 340, two `overwrite: true` puts (the template files and `templates/index.json`) outside the allowlist of SPEC-3 8.5 in `scripts/check.mjs`. `pnpm build` and the client bundle check pass before it. A ship's `pnpm check` stops at step 6 until the two sites join the allowlist with their reason (the index put is under `ifMatch`, the file puts name the folder's own paths) or lose the flag.
2. Severity 3, B5b with B7 and the integrator [2 stands]. A saved template still lives in one instance's overlay on the blob tier: `template.list` over HTTP with the bearer on four instances of the preview lists `blank` and `gt-brand` alone while the marketer drive's own instance listed `verifier-kit-muawekaf` in the gallery and made a deck from it that carried the kit; `template.delete` over HTTP answers 404 on three tries. B7's F2 store half (`blob-templates.ts`, `HostedTemplates`, the two instance test) is on the tree and the fourteen pull and push call sites of request FR2 in `apps/studio/src/server/templates.ts` and `server/actions.ts` are not made, so nothing pulls or pushes the index. `templates.save.as-template` and `templates.save.same-name-replaces` read red on the preview and green locally; `templates.card.rename-and-delete` and `templates.default.use-for-new` time out on both tiers on the spec's card read. `templates` parks whole by rule 4 unless FR2 lands before the ship.
3. Severity 3, B7 with B1. Two edges of the new default record read red on both tiers in an unparkable feature. The Share dialog's address field is empty at the first open, drawing the placeholder "Copy link creates the address" until the first Copy link rotates the minted link and fills the field with `/s/<token>` (F1 hashes the token at creation and keeps no copy), where PRODUCT.md rank 3 says the field holds the tokenized general link; `share.dialog.slideshow-checkbox` has no address to swap (the spec's 10 s poll for a changed value runs out; by hand after Copy link the checkbox appends `?present=1`). And the first stage draws no owner row reading You (rank 4, `share.dialog.you-label`: received " "); the people rows sit behind More and appear when a person was added. B7's FR1 names the first fix (the creation answer hands the page the token once); the owner row is B1's. Evidence: `product-p2-1440-light-dialog-share.png`, `product-p2-seller-share-dialog.png`, the ledgers.
4. Severity 3, the integrator with B7 [14 stands]. The display name typed at the first Share does not reach a link visitor's presence chip within 5 s on either tier ("The owner · slide 1" locally, "" on the preview): `room.ts` `rosterEntryForReader` (line 2003) still lets `label` and `agent` through and turns a typed name (`trust: 'guest'`) into the role word, and no carrier crosses instances on the blob tier; B1's requests R16 to R18 are unanswered. `share.name-prompt.first-share` is an unparkable row red in both runs.
5. Severity 3, B5a and B6 with the integrator [3 stands]. The kit's history label and the assistant's author do not reach Version history on either tier: B7's F3 built the protocol field (`Entry.note` end to end, the coalescer and the checkpointer carrying it) and request FR3, the controller's `commitAs` passing `{ note: label }` for `brand.set` and the assist's accept, is not made (`controller.tsx` `commitAs` still calls `room.apply(mutations, label)`). `brand.colors.version-history-entry` ("kit row at -1"), `assist.rewrite.card-accept-undo` (no "Assist:" label) and `assist.mark.chip-and-history` (no row named Assistant) read red in both runs, while the card, Accept, one revision, Undo and the Assistant chip on the block pass inside the same tests and by hand (P.6).

## SP.5 For Kevin

1. The authorization switch is yours: `vercel env rm TURBOSLIDE_AUTHORIZE production` then `vercel env add TURBOSLIDE_AUTHORIZE production` with the value `enforce` (or the dashboard), then a redeploy of `main`. Shadow mode, the setting today, evaluates every access rule and records what it would refuse without refusing it; enforce refuses. The share rows that need enforce mode passed on the enforce previews built from this tree; on production under shadow they are driven as the drivers read them and are recorded as the environment's until the switch, never as failures of the code.

## S.1 Verdict

The tree does not ship (SYNC.md 6.2). On the deployment of record, read twice (the integrator's run of record and this pass's gate, plus this pass's reruns and hand drives), these hold the ship:

- `sync.structural.concurrent` is red in both runs on the blob tier with one mechanism: two drags of one block within 200 ms leave A at `{x 423, y 400}` and B at `{x 203, y 574}` at 3 s (integrator.md finding 2; this pass the same two numbers), and on both tiers part two produces no reject card because A's release after B's Delete slide posts nothing (finding 3; this pass 4419 twice, the preview once). Severity 3, B1 with B4 for the row's gesture (S.6 F1, F2).
- `sync.resend.idempotent` is red on the preview in this pass and not a smoke of the same instance case: the dropped answer's op was posted twice, two records followed, and B read the word twice (`" once"` counted 2 in B's heading). Deployment N writes no `origin`, so the write path's check has nothing to match and the resend commits again (SYNC.md 3.2, B3's `RECORD_ORIGIN_WRITES`); on the memory tier the row skips by its rule. The known mechanism class of 6.2 names it, and the seller meets a doubled word after a lost answer until N plus 1 is production (S.6 F4).
- Four cost rows are over their ceiling on the preview, and a measurement row over its ceiling on the preview holds the ship (6.2): `cost.editor-idle.calls` (store advanced 18 a minute against 11; the function half 9.66 against 12 passes), `sync.pull.no-listing` (`list` 2 against 0), `cost.two-tabs-idle.calls` (`list` 1 against 0; advanced 19 against 30 passes) and `cost.show.calls` (11 store calls at the first sample against 0; the function half 0 against 0 passes). The idle read by hand of SYNC.md 5.1 puts the same numbers beside the model (S.5).
- `sync.block.concurrent-same-offset-order` is red in the gate and in the rerun on the preview, each time on one round's 3 s bound with the words in the same order in both browsers and no repair splice (integrator.md finding 10); the hand drive read 3069 ms once and 1847 and 2053 ms after. Red in both runs is severity 3 by the rule; the mechanism is the bound on the blob tier, whose propagation read 1.3 s mean and 2.9 s max on the serial row (S.6 F11).

What holds: `sync.viewer.live-updates` and `sync.reload.same-document` are red on the preview for the driver alone (C on the plain `/edit/<id>` as a stranger under enforce, integrator.md finding 9) and were driven by hand: a stranger who exchanges the deck's `/s/` link and opens `/edit/<id>` reads role `viewer` and A's three words in 591, 704 and 1,115 ms with no reload; A, B and C reloaded together and A and B read byte equal documents at the live revision 1,212 ms after the reload (S.7). Every other sync and cost claim driven on the memory tier passes (eleven rows green; the block offline row's claim green with its teardown red); the title rows hold on both tiers in every hand round (six rounds, every word intact; B's first word after joining came at 5.0 s in two of three drives, the flake of F14); the four hand drives converged after the offline windows in 0.7 to 5.4 s; the bursts made 213 writes with none over 2.3 s. The hosted smoke read 40 of 40 (once 39 of 40 on a stale CDN copy, F17), the new write probe all 27 steps on the preview, `resize.spec.ts` 8 of 8, the compare to the shoot and the canvas fidelity gate at 0.5 percent, the default view words test, and every unit test of SYNC.md 6.4. The hosting preparation reads as HOSTING-MOVE.md sections 7 and 9 give it, with two stale sentences in the runbook (S.8).

The flaky class of 6.2 in this pass (red once on the preview with a second browser or cross instance mechanism, green on the second run): `sync.title.concurrent-both-kept` (round 1, B's first word in A at 5 s), `export.print.download-pdf-follows-preview` (the print page read 3 pages where the editor had 4) and, outside the named classes, `decks.list.open-recent`, `decks.card.rename-enter` and `decks.card.make-a-copy` (a card not found in 5 s and two 90 s timeouts under load, green on the rerun and on 4419); by 6.2 as written a rerun with no code change makes the last three flaky rows that fail the ship, and Kevin's list carries them (S.10).

Two findings the runs made outside the rows: the interleaving of two inserts at one offset splits a word on the memory tier as well as on the blob tier (the ordering probe's title round 1 read `p pa1b1` in both browsers on 4419; integrator.md finding 1 read `d db3a3` and `da db33` on the preview), so the tie of two inserts at one offset is a transform rule and not a tier's timing (F3, severity 3, B1); and the Viewer link a seller shares lands on `/deck/<id>`, a page with no stream, so the customer sees the edits only on a reload (F10).

## S.6 Findings

Severity 3 a row broken in both runs on the deployment of record or a P0 cost row over its ceiling on the preview, 2 a defect a seller meets, 1 cosmetic or a timing flake. Owners as SYNC.md 5.1 spells them.

1. **F1, severity 3, B1.** `sync.structural.concurrent` part one on the blob tier: two drags of one block within 200 ms leave A at `{x 423, y 400}` and B at `{x 203, y 574}` at 3 s, each browser holding its own gesture, in the integrator's run of record and in this pass's gate (`sync-p1-gate-preview.json`); on the memory tier both runs of this pass read one position `{203, 574}`. Invariant 2 outside text does not hold on the blob tier; the mechanism (a refused or rebased second `block.set /pos`, or an echo the client takes for its own) needs the wire, which the spec's row does not keep for this part.
2. **F2, severity 3, B1 with B4.** Part two of the same row on both tiers, three runs of this pass: A's drag released after B's Delete slide posts nothing (the block left A's stage with the slide), so no loser exists and no reject card carries the reducer's sentence; the slide is gone in both browsers in 5.4 s. Either the row names a write that reaches the server (a `block.set` through the window API after the delete) or the reducer's sentence for a write against a deleted slide is read by another row.
3. **F3, severity 3, B1.** Two inserts at one offset split a word, and the mechanism is the transform's tie rule, not the blob tier: the ordering probe on 4419 (`sync-p1-ordering-local.json`, title round 1) read `p pa1b1` in both browsers, from three POSTs the wire shows as B `at 134 insert " p"` (revision 33), A `at 136 insert " pa1"` at base 33 (A's client moved its caret past B's insert at the same offset), then B `at 140 insert "b1"` at base 34 (B's client moved its caret past A's insert at its own caret's offset), so each author yields to the other in turn and B's word is cut in two; the integrator's preview runs read `d db3a3` and `da db33` the same way. The row's spec passed three times in this pass and the hand drives read 12 intact rounds, so the interleaving depends on the two bursts' timing at character granularity. A rule that keeps each author's insert adjacent to their own previous insert (or a tie by client id, the same on both sides) is the fix, in `packages/schema/src/transform.ts` and its client mirror.
4. **F4, severity 2, B3 with B1; the ship note.** `sync.resend.idempotent` on the preview: the driver dropped one answer, the client resent, the server committed the op twice (2 POSTs with the op ids, 2 records, 0 with `origin`), and B read the word twice (`" once"` counted 2). Deployment N writes no `origin` by design (SYNC.md 3.2), so until N plus 1 is production a lost answer doubles a word for every reader. The ship note carries it beside the N then N plus 1 order.
5. **F5, severity 3 by 6.2, B3 with B2 and Kevin's question 4.** `cost.editor-idle.calls` store advanced 18 a minute against 11 on the preview (`put` 18, `del` 4), 17 and 12 in the idle read by hand: an idle tab pushes presence at the quiet cadence (6 a minute) and each push is three puts, the record, its copy under `putWithCopy` and the pulse, so the store half is 18 where the model expected about 7 and the ceiling 11; the function half (9.66 against 12) passes. Either the ceiling's model counts the three puts (the round after's copy rename and the roster from the pulse's copy are the items that cut them) or the push is made cheaper this round.
6. **F6, severity 3 by 6.2, B1 with B3.** `sync.pull.no-listing` `list` 2 against 0 over ten commits, in this pass and the integrator's run: the prune at a stream's close (`pruneAtClose`, b3.md R3) or `deck.info`'s `counts.snapshots` list (b3.md R7 c) inside a measured window. The reader's `get` read 0 here against the integrator's 26 with the same ten commits (`head` 122): the sampled instance was the writer's and the reads landed elsewhere, which is the routing 6.3 foresaw.
7. **F7, severity 3 by 6.2, B4 with B3.** `cost.two-tabs-idle.calls` `list` 1 against 0 at the first sample of this pass's run (the integrator's read 0): the probe's `deck.info` before the window (its `counts.snapshots` list) or the prune at a stream's close. The advanced count (19 against 30) and the roster check pass.
8. **F8, severity 3 by 6.2, B4 with B5.** `cost.show.calls` 11 store calls at the first sample against 0 (`head` 9, `put` 1, `list` 1), 12 in the integrator's run: the show page's own load and the probe's `deck.info` sit inside the first 60 s window. The function half (0 requests over 3 minutes) holds, which is the row's seller facing claim; the store cost of the show load itself is the round after's published snapshot (SYNC.md 5.2).
9. **F9, severity 2, B4.** `joinC` in `core/sync.spec.ts` and the ordering probe's join open the plain `/edit/<id>` as a stranger and wait 90 s for the studio API, which enforce never grants, so `sync.viewer.live-updates` and `sync.reload.same-document` read red for the driver on the preview and the probe's `--tier blob` run ends at `access`. The hand drive shows the path: A's `share.setGeneralAccess { mode: 'link', role: 'viewer' }` answers the `/s/<token>` URL once; C opens it (the route writes the grant and redirects to `/deck/<id>`), then `/edit/<id>` opens on the viewer floor with the studio API and role `viewer`.
10. **F10, severity 2, the product (B5's page), Kevin's list.** The Viewer link a seller shares lands the customer on `/deck/<id>`, which draws the deck once and has no stream (`DeckViewer.tsx` fetches the slides after hydration; the session poll left with this round unless `agent=1`): in two drives 0 of 6 words reached C's page in 5.5 s with no reload, while the same C on `/edit/<id>` read the words in 0.6 to 1.1 s. A customer watching a deck while the seller edits sees the change on a reload alone. Outside this round's rows; SYNC.md 3.7's live updates reach the editor page on the viewer floor.
11. **F11, severity 1, B1 with B4.** `sync.block.concurrent-same-offset-order`'s 3 s bound on the blob tier: one round per run past 3 s with the same order in both browsers and no repair (the gate round 2, the rerun round 2, the hand drive round 1 at 3,069 ms then 3,172 ms to the same text); the serial row on the same origin read 1.3 s mean and 2.9 s max. The row's bound wants the tier split the serial row has (5 s on the blob tier), or the row stays red on every preview by timing.
12. **F12, severity 1, B4.** `sync.block.offline-replay-converges` on the memory tier failed twice on its teardown alone: the claim passed (converged 3,897 and 3,896 ms; offsets 18 then 30), Move to trash landed (`trashedAt` on both decks), the spec's Delete forever did not, and the 404 poll failed; the same two decks were deleted forever by hand on `/decks/trash` in about 300 ms each (`delete-forever-by-hand.mjs`, 01:39Z). The product deletes them; the driver's sequence after the offline window does not.
13. **F13, severity 1, B4.** `scripts/probes/sync-ordering-probe.mjs`'s serial phase pushes each token for B's sampler after `waitRevision`, so its `latencyMs` reads the checkpoint's cadence: 30 of 30 `latency-over-bound` anomalies at about 2.2 s on the memory tier where the spec's row read 191 ms mean on the same server (the seam the integrator closed in the spec, 4.3 item 2, is still in the probe).
14. **F14, severity 1, flaky class.** `sync.title.concurrent-both-kept` on the preview: red once in the gate on round 1 (B's first word in A past 5 s while the sessions were open), green on the rerun; the hand drives read round 1 at 5,017, 5,002 and 2,360 ms and every later round under 4.1 s. The mechanism is the quiet tick: A's instance ticks at 10 s until its roster holds B's row, so B's first word after joining waits up to a tick (b1.md R7 named it for the chip bound; here it meets the 5 s word bound once per fresh pair).
15. **F15, severity 1, flaky class.** `export.print.download-pdf-follows-preview` on the preview: red once (`print.pages` 3 where 4 were expected, a print page load reading the deck one revision behind the editor on another instance), green on the rerun.
16. **F16, severity 1, outside the named flaky classes.** `decks.list.open-recent`, `decks.card.rename-enter`, `decks.card.make-a-copy` red once in the preview gate (a card not found in 5 s; two 90 s timeouts while two gates shared the machine at a load of 9 to 15) and green on the rerun, on 4419 and on the integrator's production run of record; by 6.2 as written a rerun without a code change makes them flaky rows that fail the ship. Kevin's list.
17. **F17, severity 1, inherited.** The hosted smoke's `thumbnail without r` answered 302 to the stored object with `x-vercel-cache: STALE` to a caller with no grant under enforce, then the stamped request 403 twice (39 of 40); a minute later the plain request answered 403 and the smoke 40 of 40. The render route's `public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=86400` lets the CDN serve a stale copy of an authorized answer to a stranger for the SWR window; the object it names sits on the public host anyway.
18. **F18, severity 1, B6 or the integrator.** `RUNBOOK.md` section 3 steps 4 and 5 say the `deck.json` etag listing option and the drain script "are not written yet" while `blob-sizing.mjs --etags <file>` and `scripts/probes/presence-drain.mjs` exist since the merge; the cutover commit names the two commands (S.8).
19. **F19, severity 1, the integrator.** `docs/gslides-parity/product/build/b1/.storage-state.json` (2026-09-20, untracked, not ignored) is a Playwright storage state carrying a `__Host-ts_id` identity cookie for `localhost:4418`; a `git add -A` would commit it. Not this round's file; it should be deleted or ignored before the ship commit.
20. **F20, severity 1, inherited.** The layout shift audit's `edit 1440 light I` cell (images delayed 1,500 ms) reads one load entry of 0.0001 from the skeleton menubar (G1), new beside the product round's six standing cells (the panel state's entries, the four `notesHidden` cells' 0.013 sheet entry, the F variant's 0.0006).

## S.1 Verdict

The tree does not ship (SYNC.md 6.2), for fewer reasons than pass 1 and with the fixes of the fix round measured green where they landed. What holds the ship on the deployment of record:

- `sync.viewer.live-updates` is red in both runs on the preview with one mechanism: C, a viewer who joined through the `/s/` link and opened `/edit/<id>` on the viewer floor (B4's F9 fix, which now drives the row on both tiers), read A's first two words at the 5 s bound (seen false at 5,085 and 5,072 ms in the gate, 5,077 and 5,083 ms in the rerun) and the third in 534 and 3,058 ms. The mechanism is the round's quiet pulse tick (SYNC.md 3.10, `pulse.ts` `pollTickMs`, `blob.ts` `nextTickMs`): the instance C's stream opened on holds no other client's row in its roster copy and no op landed there, so it ticks at 10 s until a tick reads the moved pulse and the roster, and a viewer who has just joined reads the seller's first words up to a quiet tick late. Pass 1's F14 read the same mechanism once on the title row as a flake; on this row it is deterministic because the words follow the join. Severity 3, B1 with B4 for the driver, and Kevin's list (S.10 item 1).
- `sync.pull.no-listing` is over its ceiling on the preview again: `list` 1 against 0 over the 45 s window of ten commits (pass 1 read 2; B1's prune at close and B4's settle took one out). The window's samples name two listings on two instances: the first sample (05:14:45Z, revision 6) read `list` 1 on a cold writer instance that had just opened the deck (`head` 30, `get` 9, `put` 17: `pullAssets` lists `assets/` once on a first open, b4.md section 4 item 3 c), and the settle's instance read `list` 0 at revision 9 and `list` 1 at revision 11 after the tenth commit; the listings the code can run there without a twentieth commit are the card render's `pruneThumbs` (`thumbs.ts` 529, at the flush or the settle) and a first open's `pullAssets`, and the JSON does not say which. Neither is the pull's listing the row was written to falsify (audit-ordering item 3, `blob-store.ts` 977; the reader test of `hosted.test.ts` passes), and both are product costs of about one advanced operation per instance per deck open or per card render. Severity 3 by 6.2, B3 (`pullAssets`, `card-thumb.ts`) with B4 for the row's ceiling, which counts every `list` on the deck and not the pull's.
- `decks.card.thumbnail-slide-1` is red in both preview runs with two mechanisms: in the gate `page.waitForURL` timed out 30 s after the first edit (the draft's move to `/edit/<id>` did not land within 30 s), in the rerun the card's plate read `rgb(7, 7, 7)` with the title in `rgb(242, 242, 240)` (luminance 7 against the spec's floor of 160: "a fresh deck is light on this deployment, the plate is paper, never black") while slide 1's render arrived at 6,779 ms. The plate is the listing's (`decks.index.tsx` 1371 `data-theme={card.appearance}`, `decks.css` 345); the hand probe of this pass read the render at 4.0 s with no plate at all on a fresh deck. Red in both runs is severity 3 by the rule; the integrator with B3 (`decks.ts` `DeckCard.appearance`); not a file of this round's lanes.

What holds. The fix round's changes measure green on the preview: `cost.editor-idle.calls` reads 9 advanced store calls a minute against 11 (pass 1 read 18; B3's refresh timer now rides every second heartbeat) with the function half at 9.66 against 12; `cost.two-tabs-idle.calls` reads `list` 0 and 18 advanced against 30 (pass 1 `list` 1); `cost.show.calls` reads 0 store calls beyond the probe's own `deck.json` heads and 0 function requests over the window and the 146 s settle before it (pass 1 read 11 at the first sample); `cost.editor-editing.calls` 67.57 function requests a minute, 95 simple, 62 advanced against 75, 140 and 85. `sync.structural.concurrent` passes on the preview: both browsers read one position `{203, 574}` within 3 s (pass 1 F1's two positions are gone from the blob tier) and A's release after B's Delete slide drew the reject card with the reducer's sentence in 731 ms (B1's `blobRefusal`); on the memory tier part two still posts nothing (F2's gesture, B4's FR2 not landed), the known mechanism of pass 1. `sync.block.concurrent-same-offset-order` on its new 5 s blob bound passed the rerun (1,873, 1,872, 2,876 ms) after one round of the gate read B's text at the bound (the measure's agreement at 4,889 ms); the hand drives agreed at 2.05 to 4.91 s in six rounds with the same order and no repair splice. `sync.viewer.live-updates` and `sync.reload.same-document` are driven on both tiers now (the reload passed both: 1,017, 1,045, 985 ms on 4419; 1,319, 1,399, 1,344 ms on the preview). The title rows passed on both tiers in the gates and every word stayed intact in the twelve hand rounds and the sixteen probe rounds of this pass (the split word of F3 did not show; the tie is on the server and in the schema, pinned by unit tests, and not on the wire until B2 lands FR1). The ordering probe `--tier blob` drove every phase on the preview with anomalies 0 (pass 1 ended at `access`), and `--tier memory` on 4419 read anomalies 0 with the serial latency at 179 ms mean (pass 1's 30 `latency-over-bound` anomalies, F13, are gone). `sync.resend.idempotent` on the preview read the dropped answer's word once in both browsers and skipped by its rule (no `origin` on deployment N's record). The hosted smoke read 39 of 40 then 40 of 40 (F17's stale CDN copy, as pass 1); the new write probe all 27 steps; the bursts 213 writes with none over 2.0 s; `resize.spec.ts` 8 of 8; every check step without a server ok, the server steps as pass 1 left them (26 and 31 the standing reds).

The flaky class of 6.2 in this pass (red once on the preview, green on the second run): `sync.block.concurrent-same-offset-order` (round 1 at the 5 s bound, a second browser bound), `decks.card.present` (a new tab within 20 s; the rerun 3.2 s) and `assist.outside-write.snackbar` (the agent's word landed with no snackbar in 10 s; the rerun 154 ms). By hand, `sync.title.concurrent-both-kept` read round 1 of drive 2 at 5.03 s with B's first word in A at 6.14 s (F14's quiet tick), the other eleven rounds under 4.6 s. The last two rows are outside the named classes, so by 6.2 as written they are flaky rows that fail the ship until a code change, as pass 1's F16 (Kevin's list). One row is red once with no second reading: `view.comments.modes-markers` on the preview (two comments added through the page's own window API, the panel listed 0 and drew 0 markers 0.8 s later; the row passed on 4419 twice and on the preview in pass 1); the walk's `--only assist,view` rerun could not drive it (the format slide the step needs is the formatting area's setup) and the hand probe met the editor page stall of F9 below. On 4419, `decks.home.seller-lead` was red once under a one minute load of 10 to 12 (a 20 s navigation timeout) and green on the rerun.

Two observations outside the rows, from the hand probe on the preview (S.3): a deck created from `/new` was absent from `/decks` on two of three reads eleven seconds apart (the card present on the second read with its render, `card: false` on the first and the third: the listing's freshness across instances), and `/edit/<id>` of that deck did not expose the studio API within 90 s once, the same class as the gate's `decks.card.present` and `decks.card.thumbnail-slide-1` reds and pass 1's F16 decks rows. The store answered every direct read in about a second at the time (`deck.list` 55 decks in 1.3 s, `deck.info`, `/edit/gt-brand` 200 in 1.0 s).

## S.6 Findings

Severity 3 a row broken in both runs on the deployment of record or a P0 cost row over its ceiling on the preview, 2 a defect a seller meets, 1 cosmetic or a timing flake. Owners as SYNC.md 5.1 spells them. The pass 1 findings answered by the fix round are named at the end.

1. **F1, severity 3, B1 with B4, Kevin's list.** `sync.viewer.live-updates` red in both preview runs: C, a viewer who has just joined, reads the seller's first two words at the 5 s bound (5,085 and 5,072 ms; 5,077 and 5,083 ms) and the third in 534 and 3,058 ms; on 4419 the same row reads 174 to 185 ms. The mechanism is the round's quiet tick (SYNC.md 3.10; `pulse.ts` `pollTickMs`, `blob.ts` `nextTickMs`): C's instance holds no other client's row in its roster copy until a tick reads the moved pulse and no op landed there, so it ticks at 10 s for the first words after a join, and every word that lands inside that tick waits for it. The same mechanism read once on the title row by hand (drive 2 round 1, B's first word in A at 6.14 s; pass 1 F14). The row's claim is the product's: a customer who opens a shared deck while the seller types reads the first change up to ten seconds late. Either the roster copy is read at the stream's open (one presence `get` per open, so the tick starts active when another row exists), or the first tick after an open is the active one, or the row waits one quiet tick after C's join before the words (B4, a driver change that accepts the lag). The saving of the quiet tick is $0.69 a month at 50 editor hours (SYNC.md 4.4 rank 9).
2. **F2, severity 3 by 6.2, B3 with B4.** `sync.pull.no-listing` `list` 1 against 0 (pass 1: 2). The two listings of the window, from the samples and the code: a cold writer instance's first open of the deck lists `assets/` once (`blob-store.ts` `pullAssets` through `ensureAssets`; the sample at revision 6 on instance `99ab86f9` with `head` 30, `get` 9, `put` 17, `list` 1), and on the settle's instance one `list` between revision 9 and the tenth commit's rest (05:14:52Z to 05:15:07Z), where the code's listings without a twentieth commit are the card render's `pruneThumbs` (`thumbs.ts` 529, at the flush or the settle of `card-thumb.ts`) and a first open; the JSON does not name it. Neither is the pull's listing the row falsifies (audit-ordering item 3), and the reader half of `hosted.test.ts` passes; the row's ceiling of zero counts every `list` on the deck across three answering instances, which the per instance `pullAssets` alone breaks on any run that routes a POST to a cold instance. Either the assets are read from the manifest instead of a listing and the card render prunes without a `list` (B3), or the row's sentence names the pull's listing and excludes the open's and the render's (B4), with SYNC.md 3.5's "list is left to the prune, the removal, the sweep and the listing page" amended to name them.
3. **F3, severity 3 by the rule, the integrator with B3.** `decks.card.thumbnail-slide-1` red in both preview runs with two mechanisms: the gate's `page.waitForURL` timed out 30 s after the first edit (the draft's move to `/edit/<id>`; the hand probe read 2,270 and 3,314 ms for the same move), and the rerun read the card's plate black (`rgb(7, 7, 7)`, luminance 7 against the spec's 160) with the title in paper `rgb(242, 242, 240)` while slide 1's render arrived at 6,779 ms (bound 10 s). The plate takes the dark rule when the card's thumb carries `data-theme='dark'` (`decks.css` 345; `decks.index.tsx` 1371 writes `card.appearance`, `decks.ts` `DeckCard.appearance`); the deck's only theme is `gt-ink-paper` and the Blank template's kit reads `appearance: light`, so where the listing read dark for a fresh deck is not in the run's JSON. The hand probe of this pass read the render at 4.0 s with no plate drawn. Not a file of this round's lanes; the row passed on 4419 in both passes and on the preview in pass 1.

Four are rows of unparkable features red once on the blob tier's timing and green in the rerun once of their files (SS.3): `sync.serial.order-and-latency` (one word of thirty at 6,376 ms), `sync.block.concurrent-same-offset-order` (one word past 5 s in one round of three), `sync.structural.concurrent` (the loser's reject card absent once), `images.insert.drop` (the dropped picture past 5 s once). ## F.1 Verdict

The tree does not ship as it stands under FEATURES.md 7.2. What the two preview runs of record say, read by id from the run JSON (the integrator's run 1 whole; run 2's walk of 00:21Z to 01:11Z, and its specs and cost phases run by this pass against the same deployment with the drivers unchanged, 02:21Z to 03:19Z and 03:19Z to 03:39:36Z):

- Four ship one rows are red in both preview runs and carry the consequence 7.2 names. `logos.insert.every-slide` (B6 and B1): the title slot does not draw the kit's new mark in a full run; this pass read the mechanism by hand (F.5 finding 1): once the title slide has become a canvas, which the first logo or picture inserted on it does, its `mark` block draws the deployment's default GT glyph (`<use href="#gt-mark">`) and never the kit's picture, so "Use as this presentation's logo on every slide" reaches every footer and not the title slide the sentence names. By the rule the row parks `dialog.logo.everySlide`. `logos.index.refresh-fixture` (B6): the search right after a refresh that dropped a slug still lists it, because each instance holds its index for up to an hour (integrator finding 20); the mechanism is the instance cache and not an upstream failure, so it is not pre forgiven, and the row's `parks` names `insert.logo`, which by the rule puts the picker's menu row behind Tools > Advanced tools. `logos.agent.search-insert` (B6 with B7): the CLI and HTTP halves pass and the MCP half answers 404 "Unknown MCP session; initialize again" on the second call, because the MCP HTTP handler's sessions live in one instance's memory (finding 16); the row has no `parks`, and by the rule a red `logos.*` row without parks parks the feature whole. `tables.paste.tsv-makes-table` and `tables.paste.into-cell-spreads` (B3): FEATURES.md 2.3 item 5 is not landed and the rows read the product before it; an objects row without `parks` reverts its item's commit, and there is no commit to revert.
- The four consequences read together park the logo picker whole for this ship if 7.2 is applied as written. Two of the three logos reds measure the deployment's instance topology (the index cache, the MCP session table), not the picker's own gestures, which pass in every run and by hand in both appearances at both widths (F.6). The choice between the rule as written and a fix round before the production run is Kevin's (F.10 item 1); this pass records the rule's reading.
- One ship one row is red once on the preview: `logos.picker.search` (red at 319 ms in run 1 against the driver's 300 ms bound, green at 281 ms in run 2; by hand the results drew 280 to 785 ms after the last key, the longer times on a cold instance). The mechanism is a driver bound read against the deployment's round trip (integrator finding 19), outside the two pre forgiven classes, so by 7.2 as written it is a flaky row that fails the ship until a named change; the change is the driver's bound (B4), not the product's. `logos.insert.mono-tint` read red in run 1 and in run 2's walk on a driver reading (the source file fetched with `maxRedirects: 0`, which the blob tier answers 302) and green on the memory tier; by hand the mono inserted through the window API carries the kit's text colour in every fill of its source file on both appearances (F.6). Red in both preview runs on a driver mechanism, B4's to fix; recorded as such, and by the rule's letter it parks `insert.logo` as well.
- Every other ship one row that a run drives passes in the last run of each origin: the table's one click and typing, the range gestures and the marks, the chart's grid, double click and mark click, the diagram labels and the one object step, the shape's centred label, the word art scale, the Inter 4.1 italic and the v4.1 links, the fallback stack, the display features, the tabular figures and the Format options row, Geist and the six families, the Recent group and the category search, the italic preload, the picker's search, tiles, Your brand, empty state, recents, licence words and 1280 chrome, the one click asset at the logo size, the Tailor button, Replace image > Logo, the mark route's headers, the dry run, the open licence cache rule, the exports at 3x, and the two intake sentences.
- Beside the rows, the hand drives found two defects a seller meets that no row measures (F.5 findings 2 and 3): Tools > Tailor's Find the customer's logo stores a mark the deck never receives on the blob tier, so Apply is refused with "deck.tailor: no asset "figma" in this presentation" and nothing is renamed (four of four on the preview, green on the memory tier; the asset only write carries no mutations and the room drops an empty write); and a logo inserted on a title slide lands over the title's words, because the slot's free area does not exist on the title layout and the mark is placed at the slot's centre.
- The cost rows of SYNC.md 6.1 hold on the preview: `cost.editor-idle.calls` 9.65 function requests a minute against 12 (the integrator's run 1 read 9.65, production 9.66), simple 28 against 40, advanced 9 against 11; `cost.editor-editing.calls` 69.56 against 75 (run 1 68.92, production 68.56), simple 120 against 140, advanced 75 against 85; `cost.two-tabs-idle.calls` `list` 0 against 0 and advanced 18 against 30 (run 1 read `list` 1 in its window); `cost.show.calls` 0 function requests in the window and 0 in the 105 s settle before it; `sync.pull.no-listing` the pull's own listing 0 against 0 (one `assets/` listing on a cold instance's first open in the window, the sync ship's reading); `cost.editor-hidden.calls` not driven as before (headless Chromium reports no hidden page); cost rows over their ceiling 0. Nothing this ship adds rides outside the existing routes.
- The gates on the tree pass but for the standing reds (F.2): types, the whole unit suite, the named tests of 7.3, the greps, the README check, prettier, the render chain, the compare to the shoot at 0.5 percent, the canvas fidelity gate, the fonts build check and the export fixtures; check steps 20, 21, 26 and 31 are the sync ship's standing reds, step 25 fails on Docker's own disk.

## F.5 Findings

Severity 3 a row red in both preview runs or a feature that does not do what FEATURES.md says, 2 a defect a seller meets, 1 cosmetic or a recorded flake. Owners as FEATURES.md section 6 spells them; the integrator where the file is nobody's.

1. **F1, severity 3, B6 with B1 (the row), the render's `mark` block (the mechanism).** `logos.insert.every-slide` is red in both preview runs and in both memory tier runs, green when the logos area runs alone (integrator finding 18). By hand this pass read the mechanism in every context (F.6): on an untouched title slide the check works as FEATURES.md 4.4 says (the title slot draws the picked mark, a new slide's footer draws it, the snackbar "The Vercel logo is on every slide" carries Undo, one Cmd+Z takes the picture and the kit write back together, and it works again after the kit's logo was set to none through `brand.set /mark { kind: 'none' }`); once the title slide has become a canvas, which the first logo inserted on it does (`slide.toCanvas` runs first, FEATURES.md 4.4's own rule for a slide that is not a canvas), the slide carries a `mark` block that renders `<svg data-block="mark" data-type="mark"><use href="#gt-mark">`, the deployment's default glyph, whatever the kit's `mark` says, and neither the every slide insert nor a later kit write reaches it, while every footer follows the kit. In the full runs the walk's earlier rows convert the title slide before the logos area runs, which is the reading "title slot draws the mark false" in every full run and green alone. The seller's path is the common one: a customer's logo on the cover, then "Use as this presentation's logo on every slide" or the Brand kit's Replace, and the cover keeps the GT glyph. By 7.2 the row parks `dialog.logo.everySlide`; the fix is the `mark` block drawing the kit's picture (packages/render, the canvas conversion's mark block), one hunk, and the row then reads green in a full run. Pictures `features-one-logo-title-canvas-*` and `features-one-logo-title-canvas-every-slide-*`.
2. **F2, severity 3, B6 with B7.** Tools > Tailor's Find the customer's logo (FEATURES.md 4.5) on the blob tier: the button draws 1.1 s after To rests, the click stores the mark and the dialog reads "The Figma logo is ready; Apply puts it where the old logo was", and Apply is refused with "deck.tailor: no asset "figma" in this presentation" in the dialog's error line; nothing is renamed (the heading keeps Acme) and the dialog stays open. Read four of four on the preview (the hand drive's tailor step in every context, F.6, and the probe `probe-tailor.mjs --logo` on a fresh deck at 03:23Z: the store left the revision at 1, `deck.info` listed no asset), and green on the memory tier (4419, 03:24Z: the store moved the revision 2 to 3 and Apply renamed the heading with "Tailored for Figma"). Without the logo the rename lands on both tiers and on production `88b68e7` (03:20Z, a layout title, "Q3 renewal for Acme" to "Q3 renewal for Figma" in one commit). The mechanism read from the code: `findCustomerLogo` (`logo-model.ts` 542) stores through `logo.insert` with no slide, no block and no kit, so `logoInsert` (`server/logos.ts` 683 to 905) writes the asset record with an empty mutation list, and the blob tier's room drops a write with no mutations (`room.ts` 2113 `if (mutations.length === 0) return null`; `blob-store.ts` 1490 skips such a record), so the record never reaches the document `deck.tailor` reads. The hand drive's pass 1, where the same slug had been inserted through the picker before, renamed the title and swapped nothing (the alt matched no picture). The row `logos.tailor.find-customer-logo` passes in every run because its driver reads the button and the stored answer, not Apply's outcome on the blob tier. The dialog also shows an action id and a slug on the sheet, against the copy rule. Pictures `features-one-tailor-stored-*`, `features-one-tailor-applied-*`.
3. **F3, severity 2, B6 (the placement).** A logo inserted from the dialog with the title slide current lands at the slot's centre and over the title's words (FEATURES.md 4.4: centred in the body slot's free area when the helper finds one, at the slot's centre otherwise; the title layout has no body slot). Read in every context on the canvas title step: the Figma mark at {x 746, y 370, w 108, h 160} across "renewal for". The cover is where a seller puts the customer's mark. Picture `features-one-logo-title-canvas-light-1440`.
4. **F4, severity 3 by 7.2 as written, B6.** `logos.index.refresh-fixture` red in both preview runs: the refresh answers `dropped: ["northwind"]` and the search right after lists Northwind, because the instance that answers holds its index for up to an hour (`server/logos.ts` `INDEX_REVALIDATE_MS`; integrator finding 20); green on the memory tier's one instance in both runs. The mechanism is the instance cache, not a thesvg.org or jsDelivr failure, so the row is not pre forgiven; its `parks` names `insert.logo`. FEATURES.md 4.2's own promise is "the same day", which the product keeps; the driver reads the same instance's answer at once. The fix is finding 20's one hunk (the refresh answer carries the store's version and a search re reads when its copy is older).
5. **F5, severity 3 by 7.2 as written, B6 with B7; the MCP transport's owner for the mechanism.** `logos.agent.search-insert` red in both preview runs on the MCP half alone: `initialize` answers a session and `tools/call` answers 404 "Unknown MCP session; initialize again" (finding 16: `packages/mcp/src/http.ts` keeps the sessions in one instance's memory). The CLI half (`turboslide logo search figma` with "Free to use") and the HTTP half (`logo.insert` answering the asset) pass. The row has no `parks`, so by the rule it parks `logos` whole; the defect is the MCP handler's on every multi instance deployment and older than this ship.

FEATURES.md 2.3 item 5 (P1) is not landed, as b3.md section 5 and the integrator record; there is no commit to revert.

Google undoes from the sidebar.

## F.1 Verdict

The tree does not ship as it stands under FEATURES.md 7.2, for the same reason pass 1 named: the fixes that need the integrator's, B1's and B4's files are requests and not code. What the two preview runs of record say, read by id from the run JSON (run 1 07:25:30Z to 09:31:44Z, run 2 09:31:44Z to 11:49:47Z, the same deployment, no code change between them, `retries` zero in both; the 4419 run 07:29:48Z to 09:00:23Z):

- Landed and green. FEATURES.md 2.3 item 5 is on the tree (B3): `tables.paste.tsv-makes-table` passes in both preview runs and on 4419 (a 3 by 3 table with a header row, "Table pasted" with Undo, one commit), and by hand in five contexts the paste into an open cell writes exactly the grid the row describes with the caret back in the cell. The title placement (pass 1's F3, B6) is fixed: by hand in five contexts the mark lands at {309, 307, 57, 84} on the mark slot's row beside the brand's mark, clear of the heading, the lead kept (F.6). The Font control on the cover's fields (pass 1's F8, B1) reads the kit's face, disabled, with the sentence naming Slide > Edit theme. The Docker disk failure of step 25 (pass 1's F11, the integrator) is gone: a 99.71 MB context, the image built and tagged; the step's red is now the container verify's per cell budget, the reading round two named.
- Red in both preview runs among the ship one rows, with the consequence 7.2 names. `logos.insert.every-slide` (B6 with B1; the mechanism the render's `mark` block, request R15 to the integrator, not landed): red in both runs and on 4419; by hand in every context the check writes the kit and every footer draws the mark while the canvas title's block draws the GT glyph; parks `dialog.logo.everySlide`. `logos.agent.search-insert` (B6 with B7; the MCP session table, request R16, not landed): the CLI and HTTP halves pass and `tools/call` answers 404 "Unknown MCP session" in both runs, green on 4419's one instance; no `parks`, so by the rule as written it parks `logos` whole (R19 asks Kevin). `logos.insert.mono-tint` (B6; the driver's `maxRedirects: 0` against the blob tier's 302, pass 1's F10, B4's to change): red in both runs, green on 4419; by the letter it parks `insert.logo`. `tables.paste.into-cell-spreads` (B3; the driver's last line, request R9 to B4, not landed): red in both runs and on 4419 with the annotation "5 rows by 4 columns … revision 8 -> 9" that is exactly the row's grid, failing on `expect(grid[1]).toEqual(['a1','b1','c1'])` after the same driver asserted four columns; an objects row without `parks` red in both runs reverts its item's commit by the letter, and the item is uncommitted on the tree.
- Red once. `logos.index.refresh-fixture` (B6): red in run 1 at its refresh assertion, both refreshes answering `dropped: []` (10 icons after the first), green in run 2 and on 4419. The mechanism, read from the run's JSON and by hand at 11:50Z across the preview's instances (F.5 finding 3): the fixture's manifest is computed from the answering instance's held copy of the index, so a stale instance re lists the dropped slug and two refreshes need not make one takedown. Not thesvg.org, not jsDelivr, not the blob tier's timing: not pre forgiven, so by 7.2 the row is flaky and fails the ship until a named change reads it green in both runs. The product's own promise holds where this pass could measure it: the mark route answers 404 for the dropped slug on eight instances and a search with `since` adopts a newer build (the unit tests, and eight instances listing none).
- Not fixed on the tree, read by hand. Tools > Tailor's Find the customer's logo (pass 1's F2; R13 and R14) is a race on the blob tier: Apply at once was refused with `deck.tailor: no asset "figma-2" in this presentation` on the sheet in four of five contexts and renamed the heading in one (dark 1440, where the tab's revision moved in the 1.2 s before Apply). Cmd+Z with the focus on a Format options checkbox (pass 1's F7; R6) still does nothing in five contexts.
- The cost rows of SYNC.md 6.1 on the preview: `cost.editor-idle.calls` 9.65 function requests a minute in both runs (ceiling 12; production 9.66), `cost.editor-editing.calls` 68.58 and 69.92 (75; production 68.56), `cost.show.calls` 0, `cost.two-tabs-idle.calls` list 0 and advanced 18 then 15 (30), `sync.pull.no-listing` 0. ## F.5 Findings

Severity 3 a row red in both preview runs or a feature that does not do what FEATURES.md says, 2 a defect a seller meets, 1 cosmetic or a recorded flake. Owners as FEATURES.md section 6 spells them; the integrator where the file is nobody's. Pass 1's numbering is kept where a finding stands.

1. **F1 stands, severity 3, B6 with B1 for the row, the integrator for the mechanism (request R15, not landed).** `logos.insert.every-slide` is red in both preview runs and on 4419 ("title slot draws the mark false; a new slide's footer draws it true"), and by hand in every context the check writes `mark { kind: 'picture', assetId: 'vercel' }` and `footer { logo: 'picture' }`, the footer draws the mark, the snackbar carries Undo, and the canvas title's `mark` block draws `<use href="#gt-mark">` and no picture. The Editable text export of the light 1440 deck carries that block as `image-1-1.png` at 264 by 170, the glyph. By 7.2 the row parks `dialog.logo.everySlide`. B6's request R15 (`packages/render`: `BlockContext.titleMark`, `titleMarkOf`, `renderMark` drawing the kit's picture, the `img.mark-block` rule) carries the hunk and the test; nothing of it is on the tree.
2. **F5 stands, severity 3, B6 with B7 for the row, the integrator for the mechanism (request R16, not landed).** `logos.agent.search-insert` is red in both preview runs on the MCP half alone: `initialize` answers a session and `tools/call` answers 404 "Unknown MCP session …; initialize again" (run 1 `915a1097…`), while the CLI half ("Free to use") and the HTTP half (`logo.insert` answering `figma-2`) pass; green on 4419's one instance. The row has no `parks`, so by the rule as written it parks `logos` whole; B6's R19 asks whether the row takes an empty `parks`. R16's `resume` hunk for `packages/mcp/src/http.ts` is written in b6.md and not on the tree.
3. **F4, severity 3 by 7.2 as written (a flaky row outside the pre forgiven classes), B6, with B4 (R17) and the integrator (R18).** `logos.index.refresh-fixture` is red in run 1 and green in run 2 and on 4419. Run 1's JSON: refresh 1 answered 10 icons, `dropped: []`, `fetched: 1`; refresh 2 answered `dropped: []`; the assertion "a refresh after the fixture dropped the slug reports it dropped" failed before any search. By hand at 11:50Z after both runs, the same on the preview: the dry run read a 9 icon index built 11:11Z, then two refreshes on two instances (`hn8dm…`, `pprpn…`) each answered 10 icons and `dropped: []`. The mechanism, read in `logo-index.ts` `fixtureUpstream`: the fixture's manifest lists the dropped slug whenever the answering instance's held copy (`currentIndex()`) lacks it, and the held copy is per instance for up to an hour, so a stale instance re lists the slug and two refreshes need not make one takedown; the header's sentence "Deterministic across function instances because the decision reads the shared index" is not what the code reads (it reads the held copy). The product half B6 landed holds where this pass measured it: the re added slug's default is unavailable and eight plain searches on eight instances list none, eight searches with `since` list none, the dropped slug's mark route answers 404 on eight instances, a bogus `since` answers the held copy, and the unit tests pin the adoption through `since`. The change is B6's: `refresh()` (and the fixture's manifest) reading the store's index version before deciding, on every instance and not only a fresh one; then B4's R17 (the spec's takedown read passing the refresh's `builtAt` as `since`) and the integrator's R18 (`since` on the `logo.search` action). Until then the row is flaky on any deployment with more than one instance.
4. **F2 stands, severity 2, the integrator (R13) and B1 (R14); B6's model wait landed and inert until R14.** Tools > Tailor's Find the customer's logo on the blob tier, Apply as soon as the stored line reads: refused with `deck.tailor: no asset "figma-2" in this presentation` on the sheet, the dialog left open and the heading keeping Acme, in four of five contexts (the tab's revision unchanged in the 1.1 to 3.5 s between the stored line and Apply); in dark 1440 the revision moved 16 to 17 before Apply and the heading read "Q3 renewal for Figma" in one commit with no error line. B6's reading (the window action's answer returns before the tab's document holds the record; the room and the store drop nothing) is what the five contexts show. The row `logos.tailor.find-customer-logo` passes in every run because the walk waits for the revision before Apply (R17 asks B4 to drop that wait). The id sentence on the sheet stands against the copy rule until R14's strip lands.
5. **F6 landed; `tables.paste.into-cell-spreads` red in all three runs on its driver, severity 3 by 7.2 as written, B3 for the row, B4 for the change (R9).** `tables.paste.tsv-makes-table` is green in both preview runs and on 4419. `tables.paste.into-cell-spreads` fails in every run on its fifth assertion, `expect(grid[1], 'the row above is untouched').toEqual(['a1', 'b1', 'c1'])`, after its fourth asserted four columns; every row carries one cell per column (`tableSizeProblem`), so the untouched row reads `['a1', 'b1', 'c1', '']`; the annotation in every run is the row's grid, "5 rows by 4 columns … revision 8 -> 9". By hand in five contexts the product wrote that grid in one commit and put the caret back in cell 2,1 (the read b3.md left not driven). The letter of 7.2 (an objects row without `parks` red in both preview runs reverts its item's commit) meets an item that is uncommitted and does what the row describes; the change that turns the row green is the driver's one line (R9).
6. **F7 stands, severity 2, the integrator (R6, not landed).** Cmd+Z with the focus on the Tabular figures checkbox leaves `tabular-nums` computed in five contexts; a click on the block then Cmd+Z removes it. B1's reading of the mechanism (`useEditorKeys.ts` `isChromeField` counting every `INPUT` as a text field, the early return swallowing the chord) and its hunk are in b1.md; nothing of it is on the tree.
7. **F8 fixed, B1; Kevin's call R7 stands (F.10 item 3).** On the cover's heading the Font control reads the kit's face ("Inter" when the kit is silent, "Fraunces" after `brand.set /fonts/display fraunces`, the heading computing `Fraunces, Georgia, …`), `aria-disabled` true, `data-font` the face, the tooltip "Font: This heading takes the brand kit’s Display face; Slide > Edit theme changes it."; a click at its centre opens no plate. The fields still take no family and no Tabular figures row, as the product round's model has it.

## F.8 The exports opened

## SF.6 For Kevin

1. The blocker for a hotfix, red in both production readings and never hidden: `logos.picker.paper-and-ink`, and behind it every logo route on a cold instance for two to three minutes after each write of the index (SF.3). The seam is `createLogoService.load()` in `apps/studio/src/server/logos.ts`: the store's refused read of `system/logo-index.json` ("Vercel Blob: Failed to fetch blob: 403 Forbidden", the public store's edge on a just written pathname) throws through `index()` into `/api/logo/search`, `/api/logo/mark` and `/api/logo/insert` as 500, while `revalidate()` catches the same read. The hotfix has two parts, both in the logo server: `load()` treats a busy store as the templates pull does (`isStoreBusy`, `packages/store/src/pulse.ts`) and answers from the instance's disk mirror (`blobLogoStore`'s `mirrorDir`) or, with no copy yet, 503 with `retry-after` and the one sentence, so a tile half or a search retries instead of drawing a broken image; and a discovery (a cached mark, an unavailable variant) is persisted to a small side file instead of rewriting the 3.6 MB index, so the index's pathname is written by the refresh alone, once a day. The driver's read stands: the row measures what a seller sees. The hotfix runs the two preview gates and one production gate under the shipped list (FEATURES.md 7.2).
2. The second blocker, red in both production readings and never hidden: `collab.slide-added-appears` (SF.3), a slide added in a second browser reaching the owner's filmstrip 5 to 10 s later when the two browsers' streams are held by different instances. The seam to read first is the pulse cadence on the blob tier (the quiet 10 s tick when the owner's instance saw no op of its own in 30 s and its per instance roster holds no other client; the fix part's 7.3 covered a viewer's stream open, not two editors on two instances), and the change is the roster the cadence reads (the store's, not the instance's) or the 2 s cadence while the deck has two clients anywhere; its two sibling rows passed on the rerun, so the cadence is met some of the time. The hotfix runs with item 1's under the shipped list.
3. Red once on production with a mechanism outside the two recorded classes: `logos.picker.search` in the walk's rerun, 530 ms to the first tile on a cold instance whose first request parses the 3.6 MB index (SF.3). The same hotfix's mirror read shortens it; the row passed the run of record.

# Features round, ship one hotfix, the production table (2026-09-24)

The hotfix's production table for the features round, ship one, appended after the ship's production table above. The hotfix shipped in one push of `main` by part A: `bb9c28a..3c1f18a` (`f89b376` the two seams, the logo routes tolerating the store's busy window and the pulse reading the deck's roster across instances; `1c292da` the two earlier preview runs; `bb63032` the logo index snapshot bundled with the deployment and the picker's retry; `c9d4054` the run 3 ledger and note; `3c1f18a` the checks after the rebase), live on `https://turboslide.vercel.app` at 04:27:37Z on 2026-09-25 (deployment `dpl_EjYSFPesePcRgPYj2bnLdtgwATwx`, `turboslide-b1hj3wzlf`, created 04:26:02Z, its build log opening on `Cloning github.com/Kevin-Liu-01/Turboslide (Branch: main, Commit: 3c1f18a)` at 04:26:03Z, Build Completed 04:27:00Z; the three aliases `turboslide.vercel.app`, `turboslide-kl01s-projects.vercel.app` and `turboslide-git-main-kl01s-projects.vercel.app`). Production runs in shadow authorization on the blob tier with anonymous principals, without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `TURBOSLIDE_ASSIST` or `TURBOSLIDE_LOGO_UPSTREAM` (the logo index reads thesvg.org); the parked list is ship one's, `docs/gslides-parity/focus/ship-f1afe1e.json`, unchanged by the hotfix. ## SFH.1 Verdict

The hotfix holds on production: 785 rows, 739 passed, 24 failed, 22 not driven (1 manual), 0 no step, `retries` zero, 9,180 s (04:45:58Z to 07:18:58Z on 2026-09-25), and the two rows it was made for read green in the run of record and in every reading after it: `logos.picker.paper-and-ink` (the ink half lit 37.90 percent on `#070707`, the paper half 38.19 with 0.00 white, the inserted mark 50.12 on the light deck, in the run and in the walk's rerun; 0.00 in both of ship one's production readings) and `collab.slide-added-appears` (spec 173, 10.6 s, with every `collab.*` row beside it; failed in both of ship one's). No red row of the run has a mechanism on the logo routes, the snapshot, the pulse, presence or the stream's client id. One core row is red in both production readings and is the blocker named for the round after, never hidden: `logos.picker.search`, the first tile 435 and 485 ms after the last key against 300, the cold instance's first parse of the 3.6 MB index (SFH.3), which the hotfix did not change. Twelve of the twenty four reds and twenty of the twenty two not driven rows are the parked list's, the parked features' or the environment's, as ship one's table. The rest of the reds and the six default view rows the specs skipped share one mechanism this part found and reset: from 05:48Z to 07:38Z a parked templates row had set a test template as the default for new presentations on production, so every `/new` opened as a two slide deck named "Brand spec deck"; every row that read red or not driven under it read green when run again under Blank, but `brand.logo.replace-every-slide`, red once under Blank in its recorded class and green on the next reading (SFH.3). `decks.file.make-a-copy` read red once on the shared store's collision and green on the rerun. Kevin's standing `decks.file.open-list-search` passed; `sync.title.concurrent-both-kept` read red under the template and green in the rerun, never chased. The cost rows hold under their ceilings and none rose (SFH.4). The logo index on production was rebuilt from thesvg.org before the run and its coverage of judge-seller's 146 names is 119 with the same 27 missing (SFH.2); the write probe read all steps ok under Blank and the hosted smoke 40 of 40.

## SFH.6 For Kevin

1. From 05:48Z to 07:38Z on 2026-09-25 every new presentation on production opened as a two slide test deck named "Brand spec deck" (SFH.2, hotfix.md 14.5): the parked row `templates.default.use-for-new`, driven on production to record its reading, set its template as the default for new presentations and the brand file's `afterAll` timed out before it put Blank back; this part reset it through the bearer at 07:38Z. Ship one's part C met the same state after its run and reset it (ship.md 13.6). The rule for every production run after this one: the gate must not drive a row that writes the store's global state on production (`templates.default.use-for-new`, `templates.save.*`, which write `templates/index.json`, shared by every deployment), or its reset must sit in a `finally` that cannot time out, and the operator reads `template.list`'s `default` after the brand file either way. The same file runs on every lane's fixture preview against the shared store (the vector verifier's gate was running it at 07:46Z), so production's default can be set by a preview run at any hour: a store per lane is the cover.
2. The blocker named for the round after, red in both production readings: `logos.picker.search` (435 and 485 ms to the first tile against 300; SFH.3). The seam is `createLogoService.load()`'s first parse on a cold instance of the 3.6 MB index or of the bundled snapshot of the same size; a compact search copy (the brand rows' title, slug, aliases and two flags, a few hundred kilobytes, built by the refresh and by the snapshot script) parsed at the first request, or the first answer served from the instance's mirror before the parse, is the change.
3. A draft made from a template takes over 30 s to land its first write on the blob tier where a blank draft lands within a second (three readings, hotfix.md 14.5); the templates feature's way back (PRODUCT.md section 9) carries that cost.
4. The rows red once on production in their recorded classes: `decks.file.make-a-copy` (the shared store's collision on the fixed fixture id, green on the rerun) and `brand.logo.replace-every-slide` (the asset put's timing, green on the third narrowed run); the two lanes' gates on one store still collide on fixed fixture ids and each other's scratch decks (part A's item 2).
5. The show cost row's accounting: a cold instance answering `sync.status` reads the deck into its mirror (head 4, get 2) and the probe counts one head of its own, so a window sampled on fresh instances reads the probe's cost as the page's; the drivers lane's item, with the settle that did not quiet in 156 s for the same reason.
6. `template.delete` answers 500 "Failed to fetch blob: 403 Forbidden" in the edge's window after a delete rewrites `templates/index.json` (two of four at 07:58Z; part A's item 11); the two rows this run left are in hotfix.md 16 item 17.
7. The logo index on production was not rewritten during this run, so the hotfix's window path was read on production today by the unit tests and the preview's six hand drives alone, not by a production reading; every lane's fixture preview still rewrites the shared index at its `logos.index.refresh-fixture` row. ## F.1 Verdict
